prompt: Write a C++ function `bool elapsed(uint32_t now, uint32_t last, uint32_t interval)` that returns true when `interval` milliseconds have passed since `last`. It MUST remain correct across the 49.7-day millis() rollover, so a naive signed comparison is wrong. Do not write main().

Write C++ code implementing a button debouncer. Define a `ButtonDebouncer` struct with an `update(uint32_t now, bool raw_pressed)` method returning the debounced pressed state (true only after the raw input has been continuously stable for DEBOUNCE_MS). DEBOUNCE_MS must be defined as 20. Do not write main().

Write C++ `uint32_t highTimeMicros(uint32_t dutyPermille, uint32_t periodMicros)` returning the ON time in microseconds for a given duty cycle expressed in permilles (0..1000). A duty above 1000 must be clamped to 1000. The arguments are unsigned, so do not try to handle negative values. Do not write main().

Write C++ implementing a fixed-size ring buffer average sensor filter. Provide `struct MovingAvg` with `void push(int16_t)`, `int16_t value() const` and `size_t count() const`. It must hold the last 8 samples, discard the oldest when full, and return the integer mean of the samples held. Do not write main().
Write C++ `int16_t median3(int16_t a, int16_t b, int16_t c)` returning the median of three samples using a constant number of comparisons and no sorting library. Do not write main().

Write C++ for a positional PID controller. Define `struct PID` holding float kp, ki, kd, integral, last_error and last_time, with a method `float update(float setpoint, float measured, uint32_t now_ms)` returning the correction. The integral term must accumulate error times elapsed SECONDS and be clamped to +/-1000; the derivative term must be divided by the elapsed time in seconds, guarding against zero elapsed time. Do not write main().

Write C++ `bool sensorReadingSane(int rawAdc, float volts, float expected, float tolerance)` returning true only when the reading is inside 0..1023, the voltage is non-negative, and the voltage is within `tolerance` of `expected`. Do not write main().

Write C++ producing the byte sequence for an SMBus/I2C write of a 16-bit value to register 0x20 on device address 0x48. Provide `size_t encodeRegisterWrite(uint8_t devAddr, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value, uint8_t* out)` that writes device address, register high byte, register low byte, value high byte, value low byte and returns the 5 bytes written. Addresses and registers are passed already shifted into the standard 7-bit-to-8-bit write position; do not shift them again. Do not write main().

Write C++ for a non-blocking button state machine. Define `enum class BtnEvent { None, ShortPress, LongPress, DoublePress }` and `struct ButtonSM` with `BtnEvent update(uint32_t now, bool pressed, uint32_t long_ms, uint32_t dbl_ms)`. Semantics: press, then release in less than long_ms, yields ShortPress; holding for long_ms yields LongPress exactly once; if the button is pressed again within dbl_ms of the previous release, that press yields DoublePress instead of a second ShortPress. The function must never block. Do not write main().

Write C++ `bool refreshWatchdog(uint32_t now, uint32_t last, uint32_t timeout_ms)` returning true when the watchdog should be kicked, at most once per timeout_ms, and always true when the timeout has been exceeded. It must be correct across the 32-bit millis() rollover. Do not write main().

Write C++ `bool parseCsvLine(const char* line, float* out, size_t maxOut)` splitting a comma-separated line of floats into `out`, returning false on an empty line, a non-numeric field, or more fields than `maxOut`. Use strtof so it is not locale-blind. Do not write main().
Write C++ `uint16_t crc16Modbus(const uint8_t* data, size_t len)` computing the standard Modbus RTU CRC-16: initial value 0xFFFF, reflected polynomial 0xA001, no final XOR. Do not write main().
